facts.text: Mill Village grew along Mill Run, a stream that feeds French Creek, and its early economy centered on grazing, milk, and cheese production.
In 1862 the Atlantic and Great Western Railroad laid tracks through Mill Village, prompting a depot that became a hub for trade and traffic.
The first commercially successful oil well in the world was drilled near Mill Village, marking the town as a pioneer in the oil industry.
A historic hotel once stood on the southeast corner of Mill Village’s main intersection, reflecting the town’s early hospitality scene.
Mill Village is part of the Erie Metropolitan Statistical Area and lies just 19 miles south of Erie, connecting it to a larger urban center.
The town’s name evolved from Milltown to Mill Village after regional events, illustrating how local history shapes identity.
